```luau
--!strict
-- TutorialService: server owner of first-60-seconds tutorial state.
-- Creates the 'TutorialStep' RemoteEvent at require time; other services call notify().
-- Steps (in order): claim plot -> first cash-in -> buy Dropper 2 -> open shop -> buy tier upgrade.
-- Each step fires at most once and only in order, and increments 'tutorial_steps'.
-- If a step is stuck for STUCK_SECONDS, its hint is re-sent to the client (no counter bump).

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local TutorialConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("TutorialConfig"))
local ForgeTelemetry = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForgeTelemetry"))

local EVENTS = (TutorialConfig.EVENTS :: any) :: { [string]: string }

local STUCK_SECONDS = 15

-- One place that creates the remote.
local remote: RemoteEvent
do
	local existing = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(TutorialConfig.REMOTE_NAME)
	if existing and existing:IsA("RemoteEvent") then
		remote = existing
	else
		remote = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
		remote.Name = TutorialConfig.REMOTE_NAME
		remote.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
	end
end

type State = {
	fired: { [string]: boolean },
	done: boolean,
	startedAt: number,
	lastEvent: string?,
	lastAt: number,
}

local states: { [Player]: State } = {}

-- Ordered events the server drives; each fires at most once and only in order.
-- Keys that do not exist in the shared config are skipped.
local ORDER: { string } = {}
do
	local keys = { "CLAIMED", "CASHED", "BOUGHT", "SHOP", "TIER", "UPGRADED" }
	for _, key in keys do
		local value = EVENTS[key]
		if type(value) == "string" then
			local dup = false
			for _, existingName in ORDER do
				if existingName == value then
					dup = true
					break
				end
			end
			if not dup then
				table.insert(ORDER, value)
			end
		end
	end
end

local TutorialService = {}

local function numberFrom(inst: Instance?): number
	if inst and (inst:IsA("IntValue") or inst:IsA("NumberValue")) then
		return (inst :: IntValue).Value
	end
	return 0
end

-- Rebirths are stored in the 'Rebirths' leaderstat; owned upgrades are tracked
-- on the player as the 'UpgradesOwned' attribute (0 if nothing is recorded yet).
local function hasRebirthed(player: Player): boolean
	local stats = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	if stats and numberFrom(stats:FindFirstChild("Rebirths")) > 0 then
		return true
	end
	local attr = player:GetAttribute("Rebirths")
	return type(attr) == "number" and attr > 0
end

local function ownedUpgrades(player: Player): number
	local attr = player:GetAttribute("UpgradesOwned")
	if type(attr) == "number" then
		return attr
	end
	return 0
end

local function isActive(player: Player, state: State?): boolean
	if not state or state.done then
		return false
	end
	if os.clock() - state.startedAt > TutorialConfig.TOTAL_SECONDS then
		state.done = true
		return false
	end
	return player.Parent == Players
end

function TutorialService.notify(player: Player, eventName: string)
	local state = states[player]
	if not state or not isActive(player, state) then
		return
	end
	local nextEvent: string? = nil
	for _, name in ORDER do
		if not state.fired[name] then
			nextEvent = name
			break
		end
	end
	if nextEvent == nil or eventName ~= nextEvent then
		return
	end
	state.fired[eventName] = true
	state.lastEvent = eventName
	state.lastAt = os.clock()
	ForgeTelemetry.count("tutorial_steps", 1)
	remote:FireClient(player, eventName)

	-- all server-driven steps finished
	local allDone = true
	for _, name in ORDER do
		if not state.fired[name] then
			allDone = false
			break
		end
	end
	if allDone then
		state.done = true
	end
end

-- The client may report steps only it can observe (e.g. opening the shop).
-- Only the in-order next step is accepted, so spoofing gains nothing.
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player, eventName: any)
	if type(eventName) ~= "string" then
		return
	end
	if eventName ~= EVENTS.SHOP then
		return
	end
	TutorialService.notify(player, eventName)
end)

local function setup(player: Player)
	if states[player] then
		return
	end
	local state: State = {
		fired = {},
		done = false,
		startedAt = os.clock(),
		lastEvent = nil,
		lastAt = os.clock(),
	}
	states[player] = state

	task.spawn(function()
		-- leaderstats may not exist yet; wait briefly, then give the client time to load.
		player:WaitForChild("leaderstats", 5)
		task.wait(1.5)
		if states[player] ~= state or player.Parent ~= Players then
			return
		end
		if hasRebirthed(player) or ownedUpgrades(player) >= TutorialConfig.SKIP_UPGRADES then
			state.done = true
			remote:FireClient(player, EVENTS.SKIP)
			return
		end
		remote:FireClient(player, EVENTS.START)
		-- The plot is auto-claimed shortly after joining, so the "walk to a CLAIM gate"
		-- step would contradict the game. Advance right away via the claimed event.
		-- notify() counts tutorial_steps and is ignored if a manual claim already advanced.
		if ORDER[1] then
			TutorialService.notify(player, ORDER[1])
		end
		state.lastAt = os.clock()

		-- Stuck-step fallback: re-show the current hint if nothing advanced in 15s.
		while states[player] == state and isActive(player, state) do
			task.wait(1)
			if states[player] ~= state then
				break
			end
			local last = state.lastEvent
			if last and not state.done and os.clock() - state.lastAt >= STUCK_SECONDS then
				state.lastAt = os.clock()
				remote:FireClient(player, last)
			end
		end
	end)

	task.delay(TutorialConfig.TOTAL_SECONDS + 2, function()
		if states[player] == state then
			state.done = true
		end
	end)
end

local started = false

function TutorialService.start()
	if started then
		return
	end
	started = true
	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(setup)
	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
		states[player] = nil
	end)
	for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
		setup(player)
	end
end

return TutorialService

TutorialService (this file) and TutorialFlow (added later, it owns steps 1-6, the beam, the target and the stuck re-show) both publish step text to the client. AI testers saw the banner flip back to 'Walk to the CLAIM gate!' after the plot was claimed, and tutorial_reshown hit 70-130 per round. Make TutorialFlow the single owner. ## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Also keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price, so the shop and later upgrades get exercised.
- Starting cash must be strictly below the first upgrade's price, never equal to it. An instant spend gives the player no chase and no sense of what cubes are for. Start slightly below the price so the first few collected cubes earn it, within about 10s. Check starter cash against the first cost in config before finishing.
- The first purchase must actually happen in a short playtest, and its counters (e.g. upgrades_bought) must be above 0. If the report lacks them, the first pad is too hard to find or reach. Put it close to the claimed plot's spawn point, off the walking path, and guide the player to it with a beam. Make sure the tutorial step that points to it fires.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Give failure feedback as well as success feedback. A pad, button, shop purchase or rebirth attempted without enough cash needs a red flash, an audible buzz and a "Need $N" toast, debounced to about 1s. A silent denial confuses young players.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally. They must still be easy to find and reach: guide the player to the first pad with a visible beam or arrow.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~6-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback should fire within a few seconds (about 3-5s, not 20s), and claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. An idle player must still reach the loop quickly. Keep the spec's auto-claim delay and the tested window consistent so the plaza state can still be observed before the claim.
- Budget the whole first-payout path, not just the claim: claim delay + first spawn + conveyor travel (length / speed) should land the first cash-in within about 3-4s of the claim. Use a short, fast conveyor, spawn the first item immediately on claim, and don't leave this borderline.
- Keep tutorial text consistent with the actual flow (e.g. don't say "walk to a gate" if auto-claim happens within seconds). Tutorial steps must be advanced by events that actually occur, or the player is left without guidance. Add a time-based fallback so a step can't stall. A tutorial_reshown counter above 0 means a step stalled. Give a clear objective from second 0, make the steps lead the player to every key feature (buy pad, shop), and check that the guide beam or arrow actually appears (its census count is above 0). If the census shows beams = 0, the guide is invisible: fix the beam creation (attachments, parenting, target lookup), not just its config.
- Feedback should be audible and visible: use verified sound ids from the shared asset table, not weak built-in rbxasset wavs. Add particles or ambient sparkle, and set the bloom threshold low enough that Neon parts glow.
- Shared effect helpers (burst, shake, sound, FOV punch) only matter if gameplay code calls them. Wire each helper to a real event (collect, buy, rebirth, big upgrade) and check that its counter is above 0 after a playtest. ```luau
--!strict
-- TutorialService: thin compatibility shim.
-- TutorialFlow is the single owner of tutorial state, banner text, beam, target and
-- stuck re-show. This module keeps its public API (start, notify, onPlotClaimed) so callers
-- do not change, but only forwards to TutorialFlow. It fires no step events of its own
-- and does not bump 'tutorial_steps'.

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local TutorialService = {}

-- Lazy require so a require cycle between the two modules can never deadlock at load time.
local flowModule: any = nil

local function getFlow(): any
	if flowModule == nil then
		flowModule = require((script.Parent :: any):WaitForChild("TutorialFlow", 10))
	end
	return flowModule
end

local started = false

function TutorialService.start()
	if started then
		return
	end
	started = true
	local flow = getFlow()
	if flow and type(flow.start) == "function" then
		flow.start()
	end
end

function TutorialService.notify(player: Player, eventName: string)
	local flow = getFlow()
	if flow and type(flow.notify) == "function" then
		flow.notify(player, eventName)
	end
end

-- Called when a player's plot is claimed (manual or auto). Forwarded to TutorialFlow.
function TutorialService.onPlotClaimed(player: Player)
	local flow = getFlow()
	if not flow then
		return
	end
	if type(flow.onPlotClaimed) == "function" then
		flow.onPlotClaimed(player)
		return
	end
	if type(flow.notify) == "function" then
		local eventName = "CLAIMED"
		local cfgModule = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("TutorialConfig")
		if cfgModule and cfgModule:IsA("ModuleScript") then
			local ok, cfg = pcall(require, cfgModule)
			if ok and type(cfg) == "table" then
				local events = (cfg :: any).EVENTS
				if type(events) == "table" and type(events.CLAIMED) == "string" then
					eventName = events.CLAIMED
				end
			end
		end
		flow.notify(player, eventName)
	end
end

return TutorialService
